label: Landing page (React)
description: A landing page in React with Vite, from a working starter with a real look: design tokens, light and dark, phone to desktop. Needs Node.js.
task: Make this landing page with React in this empty folder (Node.js is installed). Make the home page the landing page: a hero (headline, one line of support, the main call to action), the sections the request needs (for example what is offered, how it works, a sign-up or contact section), a place for a customer's words marked [Fill in: a customer's words] (never made up) and the footer. Keep About only when it helps; every button and link goes somewhere. Dim Factory already put a working starter here (Vite, React and TypeScript): read docs/starter.md first, keep its structure and adapt it to the request: the words in src/content.ts, the pages in src/pages/ and src/App.tsx, the look in src/styles/tokens.css. First run npm install with no package names; add a package only when the request needs one (npm install <name>). Keep what the starter has: design tokens for every colour, size and corner, in light and dark, with at least 4.5:1 contrast for text; a layout that works from a 360 px phone to a wide screen; real navigation (src/lib/router.tsx) with a skip link, visible focus and landmarks; loading, empty and error states for anything that loads (src/components/States.tsx); the not-found page. Write every word in the language of the request, and set <html lang> on every page to that language. No lorem ipsum: write real, specific words for the request, and never invent the owner's facts (prices, hours, addresses, testimonials): keep each as [Fill in: ...] and list them in the README under Things to fill in. Pictures: keep the marked image slots (src/components/ImageSlot.tsx, assets/README.md) instead of stock photos. Nothing comes from other websites (no hot-linked fonts or images, no CDN), and there are no trackers, ads or analytics. Publish-ready: fill in the title, the description and the social preview tags in index.html; keep public/favicon.svg, public/social-preview.png, public/_redirects and the 404.html copy the build makes. No secret key goes in the page or in a VITE_ variable. Keep and extend src/App.test.tsx (Vitest) for each page and what it does. npm test and npm run build must pass, and Dim Factory opens the built page in dist/ to check that it loads without console errors, so run npm run build before you finish. Add a .gitignore for node_modules and dist, and a README.md: what it is, how to open it (npm install, then npm run dev), how to build it for sharing (npm run build makes dist/), Things to fill in, and credits (the starter from Dim Factory, MIT).
